premise: Rover wonders why the Moon is covered in round holes; Geologist tells a Just So tale about freckles, then the true one, as an asteroid tumbles past far away.
inspiration: Kipling's Just So Stories, turned: the made-up tale and the true one side by side, and you're allowed to love both.
lesson: Wonder and knowing can live together.
learning: Craters were made by rocks from space thumping into the Moon long ago.

en-US.title: How the Moon Got Its Freckles
en-US.text: {rover:enter} Rover stopped beside a small, round hole in the dust. {rover:pulse} Beep? It had a question. Why is the Moon covered in holes? {geologist:enter} {geologist:face happy} Geologist sat down. [softly] Once upon a time, he said, the Moon's face was smooth. Then the Sun told her a joke, and she laughed so hard she got freckles, all over. {rover:wobble} {robodog:enter} {robodog:face surprised} Robo-dog tilted his head. [laughs] {geologist:shake} That's the made-up story, said Geologist. {geologist:pulse} Here's the true one. Long, long ago, rocks from space came flying and thumped into the Moon, and every thump made a crater. {asteroid:enter} Far, far away, an asteroid tumbled past, {asteroid:live} minding its own business. {rover:live} Rover drilled a tiny sample from the freckle. {geologist:live} Geologist studied it. {geologist:face happy} [curious] So which story is true? beeped Rover. The second one, said Geologist. {robodog:face happy} {robodog:hop} But I like the first.

es-ES.title: Las pecas de la Luna
es-ES.text: {rover:enter} Róver se paró junto a un agujero pequeño y redondo en el polvo. {rover:pulse} ¿Bip? Tenía una pregunta. ¿Por qué la Luna está llena de agujeros? {geologist:enter} {geologist:face happy} Geólogo se sentó. [softly] Érase una vez, dijo, que la cara de la Luna era lisa. Entonces el Sol le contó un chiste, y ella se rio tanto que le salieron pecas por todas partes. {rover:wobble} {robodog:enter} {robodog:face surprised} Perro robot ladeó la cabeza. [laughs] {geologist:shake} Esa es la historia inventada, dijo Geólogo. {geologist:pulse} Esta es la de verdad. Hace muchísimo tiempo, llegaron rocas del espacio y chocaron con la Luna, y cada choque dejó un cráter. {asteroid:enter} Muy, muy lejos, pasó un asteroide dando vueltas, {asteroid:live} a lo suyo. {rover:live} Róver taladró una muestra diminuta de la peca. {geologist:live} Geólogo la estudió. {geologist:face happy} [curious] ¿Y cuál de las dos es verdad? pitó Róver. La segunda, dijo Geólogo. {robodog:face happy} {robodog:hop} Pero a mí me gusta más la primera.
